principles: Brand consistency: the product is Lattice — the scope is @lattice, not @lattice-agent.
Atomic self-host flip: rename names, workspace, bin, dist, and every self-host gate together so the running CLI never sees an inconsistent identity.
Real install, not symlink: the @lattice/* workspace links must actually exist.
Clean break on legacy: retire the @koala-agent (and @lattice-agent) global fallbacks; one canonical @lattice/core.
Keep the guards: anti-residue checkers stay and tighten to forbid both legacy scopes.
drivers: Self-host gates (pre-push build+tsc, codex verify, rollout) must run against the REAL package name, not silently pass on a stale one.
npm workspace resolution + the CLI's own package identity are load-bearing and self-modifying.

options.name: atomic-rename-drop-legacy
pros: Single consistent end state: @lattice/core everywhere; pre-push gate restored; one canonical global candidate.
Matches the operator directive exactly; no half-migrated dual-scope world.
cons: Wide change (68 refs/37 files) + npm install + rebuild; merge-conflict-prone vs concurrent main churn.
Self-host bootstrap risk: must rebuild + reinstall before the worktree gates trust the new name.
Drops migration fallback for anyone with a legacy global @koala-agent/@lattice-agent install (mitigated: heartbeat-only, not a gate; documented).

options.name: rename-keep-transitional-fallback
pros: Keeps @lattice-agent/core (and maybe @koala-agent/core) as a global migration fallback for one release.
cons: Leaves a legacy scope name live -> anti-residue/grep-clean acceptance can't be clean; contradicts the 'clean break' the operator wants.
More moving parts in the self-host detection.

options.name: defer-pre-push-only
pros: Tiny; just fixes the broken pre-push gate now.
cons: Does not deliver the operator's actual ask (@lattice scope).

rationale: It is the only option that delivers the operator's @lattice end state with consistent self-host gates and a clean grep-clean acceptance. Keeping a transitional fallback contradicts the clean-break directive and muddies the residue guards; pre-push-only doesn't deliver the rename. The legacy global fallback is heartbeat-only (not a gate), so dropping it is safe and documented.

preMortem.scenario: npm workspace resolution breaks after the rename: node bin/lattice.js can't resolve @lattice/core, so the worktree's own lattice gates (validate/advance) fail.
preMortem.trigger: package.json renamed but node_modules/@lattice/* links not regenerated, or a cross-dep version mismatch, or dist not rebuilt.
preMortem.consequence: The story can't run its own workflow gates; self-host bootstrap is broken mid-DEV.
preMortem.mitigation: After renaming the 3 package.json names+deps, run a REAL `npm install` at root, rebuild (main then utils then lab), and verify `node bin/lattice.js --version` + `rollout check` before relying on any gate. No symlinked node_modules.

preMortem.scenario: A self-host gate keeps a stale name and silently breaks or silently passes.
preMortem.trigger: One of CANONICAL_CORE_PACKAGE_NAME / rollout-check / codex-adapter-checks / .githooks/pre-push left at @lattice-agent or @koala-agent.
preMortem.consequence: pre-push skips build+tsc again, or codex-verify/rollout mis-detect self-host.
preMortem.mitigation: Enumerate every self-host name site (the touchpoints list) and flip together; acceptance runs pre-push's build+tsc path, codex verify, rollout check, and greps for any residual @lattice-agent/@koala-agent live name.

preMortem.scenario: A live @lattice-agent reference is missed (string literal / path join / doc), so residue remains.
preMortem.trigger: The change relies on enumerated files and misses one (e.g. prompt-registry.ts / init-assets.ts string).
preMortem.consequence: Residual brand inconsistency; verify-koala-residue or a manual grep later flags it.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-004 acceptance is a repo-wide `git grep -nE '@lattice-agent' -- ':(exclude).lattice/**'` == 0 live (only justified anti-residue assertions), plus updating the verifiers to forbid the live scope.
